The Bulut Doctrine.definition: A research program modeling narrative as a physical system, encoding emotional states through measurable physical parameters rather than subjective labels.

Narrative Engineering.definition: Parametric and structural modeling of narrative systems using measurable physical variables.

Objective Projection.definition: A parametric methodology encoding emotional states through six measurable physical variables instead of cortical emotion labels, targeting the pre-cortical thalamo-amygdala pathway.

Narrative Entropy.definition: Quantifies structural complexity and disorder within a narrative system, formally compared against Shannon entropy (H).

Information Friction.definition: The resistance information encounters within a narrative system; one of the two scored dimensions of the Sn Measurement Protocol v1.0.

Causal Branching.definition: The multiplication of causal pathways within a narrative system; the second scored dimension of the Sn Measurement Protocol v1.0.

Narrative Gravity.definition: Assigns mathematical mass to narrative elements in high-entropy systems; a deterministic break from the MacGuffin, later revised under probabilistic convergence.

Narrative Inertia.definition: The persistence of established narrative trajectories over time; the temporal dimension of the doctrine.

Summarization Bias.definition: Systematic distortions introduced when machine systems, including LLMs, compress narrative and journalistic material into summaries, deleting the physical matrix and substituting emotion labels.

Universal Biological Interface.definition: A post-digital protocol treating the reader's autonomic system as a universal interface for physical narrative parameters.

Two-Pathway Architecture.definition: Explains why cultural variation does not falsify the UBI: the fast thalamo-amygdala pathway responds to physical parameters, while the slow cortical pathway carries cultural interpretation.

Objective Projection Calibration Test.definition: A neurobiological and methodological framework for empirical verification of physics-based narrative construction; v2.0 tests biophysical output convergence across multiple authors.

News Physics.definition: A physical model of journalism practice, with a founding manifesto and case-analysis scoring rubric.

Physics of Literature.definition: Applies physical variables to literary systems through case studies from Werther to The Stranger and Pulp Fiction.

Biophysical Output.definition: The measurable autonomic response produced by a physical matrix, as distinct from a cortical emotion label.

Narrative Momentum.definition: The temporal dimension of Objective Projection: the quantity a narrative trajectory carries forward from scene to scene.

Narrative Memory Evolution.definition: How physical matrices persist, decay, and transform in reader memory after exposure.

Narrative Ecosystem Dynamics.definition: The social propagation layer of Objective Projection: how narratives sustain trajectory across populations and platforms.

Reader-State Interaction.definition: When the reader's context modifies the physical matrix and its biophysical output.

Reader Process Layer.definition: Extends Objective Projection beyond biophysical output into memory, context, and social propagation.

Vacuum Variable.definition: The structural void in a high-entropy system toward which narrative mass migrates.

The Ng Operator.definition: The mathematical formalization and operational definition of Narrative Gravity.

Objective Projection Dataset.definition: 500 annotated narrative scenes labelled for the six golden rules, with a bilingual detection pipeline and hard negatives.
